gap: No result ChatGPT got gives any power bank's price. Today two 25,000 mAh laptop banks cost $79.99 at their makers' own stores: Baseus EnerFill FC41 (145 W, two built-in cables) and UGREEN's 145 W 3-port. That is $20 less than the $99.99 UGREEN Nexode 20,000 mAh 165 W retractable bank ChatGPT called best overall, which holds less.
standout_why: I compared against RuntimeWise's 'Airline Power Bank and Battery Rules (2026)' (runtimewise.com, top non-FAA result), which says outright that it gives no prices and names only banned or restricted models. The FAA PackSafe pages in the results are rules pages with no products. I could not read the cited IATA power-bank PDF: its text did not extract, and pdftotext needed approval. I could not open the cited aa.com restricted-items page (HTTP 403). Going by their titles they are rules documents, and none of the results prices a single model. ChatGPT's prices appeared only in its own answer cards. They were not in any source, and two of them no longer match the maker's store.
decides: Price changes the best-overall pick. For a laptop flyer, the Baseus EnerFill FC41 25,000 mAh 145 W at $79.99 (our product) and the UGREEN 145 W 25,000 mAh at $79.99 hold more than ChatGPT's $99.99 UGREEN 20,000 mAh 165 W, and FC41 also has built-in cables. That makes the $99.99 pick hard to defend. Anker's 45 W A1638 is still $59.99 at anker.com. INIU's own store sells 10,000 mAh 45 W banks from $23.99 (Pawsible). The 99.5 Wh-plus banks cost the most: Anker Prime 26K at $229.99 and EcoFlow RAPID Pro 27,650 at $154.99 (our page still says $175.99). They buy roughly 10 Wh over the 25K picks and come within 0.5 Wh of the 100 Wh line.

findings.label: Airline per-passenger and in-flight limits
findings.value: 12 of 15 airlines checked restrict in-flight use or charging. Most allow two power banks per passenger; Emirates allows one. ICAO two-bank limit from 2026-03-27. IATA says the allowance for 100–160 Wh banks with operator approval ends in DGR 68th edition, effective 2027-01-01. Air Canada bans Anker A1647, A1681 and A1689. American prohibits large power banks from EcoFlow, Jackery and Bluetti. The page gives no prices.
findings.source_title: Airline Power Bank and Battery Rules (2026) | RuntimeWise
findings.note: This is the rival page I compared against. It names banned models but prices none.
